symptoms: High risk wound factors: extensive contamination, crush with devitalized tissue, puncture, bites to hands/wrist/feet/face/genitalia, wounds penetrating bone/joints/tendons/neurovascular structures, delayed presentation > 8 hrs.
High risk patient factors: immunocompromised, malnourished, diabetes mellitus, haem-oncology, post-splenectomy, autoimmune disease.

management_steps.details: Wash thoroughly with large volume water + soap. Extensive high pressure irrigation. Debridement of devitalized tissue (especially jagged wounds). Assess wound + rabies risk (refer to Rabies PEP protocol). Check vaccination status: ATT booster if required.

Suturing for haemostasis is required (local anaesthetic given from inside wound). Suturing for cosmesis (eg face) is acceptable (may require referral to Plastics). If wound < 8 hours + thoroughly cleaned, may be sutured (ideally loose sutures, just opposing edges to allow for swelling). If wound > 8 hours: avoid suturing + L/A.

Antibiotic prophylaxis based on risk (polymicrobial infections). Discharge advice: health education about appropriate wound care, signs of infection/cellulitis/sepsis, strict instructions to return if any concerns.

warnings: If wound > 8 hours: avoid suturing + local anaesthetic.
